A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KRAMABENCH and retain the same core benchmark and evaluation framework. All 25 pages of v2 and 30 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable and support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies are addressed in the affected judgments.

before.justification: v2 reports original system evaluations, sampling and iteration ablations, obscured-input experiments, and failure analyses in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports updated system evaluations and adds multi-agent results, a nine-participant human baseline, and a human–LLM evaluator agreement study.

M1.justification: DS-Guru's sampling, prompting, and execution-feedback procedure remains unchanged. Appendix C.3 adds a procedural adaptation of AutoPrep in smolagents PDT: non-tabular parsing tools and hierarchical task decomposition, organized into planner/decomposer and tool-executor agents. This is a limited methodological addition within the baseline suite.

E1.justification: The underlying 104 tasks, 633 subtasks, 1,764 files, and six domains remain unchanged. v2 evaluates obscured inputs on a legal/wildfire subset covering approximately 20% of tasks. v3 Section 4.1 says all tasks, but its introduction still says 20%, and Table 7 removes domain breakdowns. The actual expansion of obscured-input coverage is unresolved.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated smolagents Reflexion and PDT baselines and a human comparator (Tables 5 and 11), plus Claude-3.7 configurations for DS-Guru. Older smolagents GPT-4o/Claude-3.5 results remain in Appendix A. However, Claude-3.5 and Qwen comparisons for pipeline design and subtask implementation disappear from Table 8 and are not restored elsewhere.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a nine-participant human evaluation requiring assigned-task notebooks and staged time logs (Appendix F), and a three-reviewer audit of approximate-answer evaluations from 12 DS-Guru configurations (Appendix G.2). Table 12 adds accuracy normalized by runtime and input/output tokens. Existing Full, Oracle, Trimmed, and answer-scoring definitions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds six-domain trace-based failure analysis (Appendix D.1), a human-error taxonomy (Appendix F), automatic-judge validation (Appendix G.2), and cost–accuracy analysis (Table 12). The obscured-input analysis includes new agents. The original row-sampling and iteration ablations and two environmental case studies are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 provides point estimates without specifying repeated-run counts. v3 first reports three executions where possible, means and standard deviations, and exceptions attributed to cost or discontinued models. Appendix G.2 also reports three judge executions and Cohen's kappa for inter-human, inter-LLM, and human–LLM agreement. This does not establish that v2 used only one run.

E6.justification: Many reported scores change. Table 5 replaces Full-setting DS-Guru/GPT-o3 few-shot 22.08% with 24.98±1.25%, and smolagents DR/Claude-3.7 50% with 55.83±3.41%, now reported as repeated-run summaries. New Full results include Reflexion at 55.37±3.36% and humans at 76.75%. v3 also introduces inconsistencies: smolagents DR/GPT-o3 scores 28.07% in Table 5 but 7.57% in Table 9; OpenAI DR remains 52.18% in the tables despite prose attributing smolagents' 58.12% to it.

T1.justification: The task-score averaging and key-functionality coverage definitions in v2 Appendix E and v3 Appendix G are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations appear. The added kappa analysis is empirical statistical validation.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and central claim that current systems struggle with end-to-end pipelines remain. v3 broadens the abstract's finding to evaluated single- and multi-agent systems and adds an introductory claim that simple evaluator-style coordination provides little benefit. These extend the existing claims without redefining the benchmark's purpose.

C2.justification: v3 adds domain-specific explanations involving file formats, joins, and statistical reasoning, and more strongly associates Claude's obscured-input failures with parametric knowledge. Appendix F interprets human errors as evidence of ambiguity and pipeline-design difficulty and proposes clarification or explicit alternative assumptions. This materially qualifies v2's expectation that experts could solve tasks without additional clarification, although that expectation remains in v3.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents code actions, the Magentic-One text inspector, and agent/tool arrangements for the evaluated systems. Appendix F adds notebook submission and time-recording requirements. DS-Guru's prompt and artifact-access information remain unchanged. Conversely, v2's explicit 20-iteration smolagents cap is no longer stated; an actual budget change is not established.

R1.justification: v3 adds Reflexion and Magentic-One references and positions PDT as an adaptation of the already cited AutoPrep. The related-work taxonomy, benchmark comparison in Table 1, and overall novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and much existing prose are retained. The title, selected abstract/introduction passages, experimental setup, and takeaways are revised. Baseline, human-study, and judge-validation subsections and acknowledgments are added, with corresponding appendix renumbering.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 1 and adds six workflow, architecture, and evaluation diagrams (Figures 2–4 and 6–8); the earlier Figure 2 becomes Figure 5. Tables 2/3 and 6/7 are placed side by side, result tables are restructured for comparators and uncertainty, and Table 7 replaces domain blocks with aggregate columns. Cost and agreement tables are added.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical calibration by supplying run variability, human reference performance, and direct validation of approximate-answer judging, all absent from v2. These additions help assess benchmark difficulty and scoring reliability. The net gain is limited by new reporting conflicts, including inconsistent smolagents scores across Tables 5/9, incorrect OpenAI score attribution, and contradictory obscured-input coverage, which weaken confidence in some revised comparisons.
